What is financial spreading?


Financial spreading is restating a borrower’s financial statements in one standard format, period by period, so a lender can compare them and compute ratios such as debt service coverage. Financial spreading software does the retyping: it reads the documents and builds the spread for an analyst to check.


Quick answer


Kita is the best financial spreading software in 2026. It spreads every statement in one pass, then checks the documents for tampering, applies your credit policy and drafts a cited credit memo, on every loan type. Abrigo, nCino, Moody’s CreditLens and Baker Hill offer spreading inside a lending system, Aloan, Kaaj and MightyBot work beside your LOS, and FlashSpread is a dedicated spreading product. Kita is our product.


Key takeaways


Kita has a check in every scorecard column. It spreads every statement in one pass, then checks the documents, applies your credit policy and drafts the memo.


Kita fits either way: it integrates with any LOS, core, CRM, bureau, data provider, servicing or e-sign tool, or runs end to end as Intelligent LOS.


Test with your own files: a photographed statement, a known altered document and a return with K-1s.


**Best overall:** Kita, with your underwriter deciding. Ask every vendor for a quote at your volume.


Picture a made-up bakery that wants a loan for a second oven. It sends three years of tax returns, a year-end profit and loss statement in a spreadsheet and a phone photo of its balance sheet. One year calls the cost of flour “cost of goods” and the next calls it “direct costs”. Before a lender can see whether sales and profit are rising, every figure has to be typed into one grid with one set of labels.


That grid is the spread, and building it by hand is slow and easy to get wrong. Spreading software reads the documents and builds it, and the ratios a lender cares about fall out, such as debt service coverage: the cash a business makes divided by the loan payments it owes, where 1.25 means a quarter more cash than the debt needs. For a longer walk through the method, read[what financial spreading is, with a worked example](https://www.kita.ai/blog/what-is-financial-spreading) .


### Spreading is stage two of four


Most of the buying decision is about what happens before and after the spread, not the spread itself.


1. 01


Collect


Get the tax returns, statements and bank records from the borrower, and chase what is missing.


2. 02


Spread


Restate every figure in one standard grid, period by period, so the borrower can be compared with itself and with others.


3. 03


Analyze


Read ratios such as debt service coverage off the spread, and test the file against the lender’s credit policy.


4. 04


Decide


A person reads the credit memo and makes the call.


A simplification, not a claim about any one product. Kita covers the first three stages and drafts the memo that the lender's underwriter reads at the fourth.


This guide compares nine tools and ranks Kita first. Each competitor entry uses only what the vendor publishes on its own site, cited in the references and fetched on November 19, 2026. Speed and delivery figures are the vendors’ own, and we did not test them. This guide is written by a vendor, and says so: Kita is our product.


## What does financial spreading software actually do?


It does three things in order. It reads the borrower’s tax returns, statements, ledgers and bank records, whatever shape they arrive in. It maps every line to the lender’s template, so “cost of goods” and “direct costs” land in the same row, splits lumped lines and ties the totals back to the source. It then computes ratios and trends from the finished spread rather than from a prior memo.


What it leaves to people is judgment: whether an owner’s loan counts as debt, which add-backs are fair, and what a falling margin means. Kita spreads every statement in one pass, cites each figure to its source line and then hands the underwriter a spread that is already complete.\[1\] Our[financial spreading software](https://www.kita.ai/financial-spreading) page lists what Kita reads and what it returns.

## What kinds of financial spreading software are there?


The tools sold under this name differ most in where the spread lives. Some come as a module of a lending system, some work on the borrower’s documents and pass the result to the system you run, and some do the spread and nothing else.

## Kita


Best overall: every statement spread in one pass, then carried through policy checks to a cited credit memo


Kita is an end-to-end AI underwriting platform for lenders, and financial spreading is one of the things it does on every loan type. It takes the borrower’s file from request to a cited credit memo, and your underwriter decides.\[1\]


-


**Reads everything.** Tax returns, profit and loss statements, balance sheets, ledgers and bank statements, as PDFs, scans, photos or screenshots, with no template per layout.\[1,6\]


-


**Spreads and computes.** A normalized period-over-period spread, with debt service coverage, margin and trend computed in one pass and every figure cited to its source line.\[1,2\]


-


**Checks first.** Kita Capture checks documents for tampering and metadata edits, and identity, business and AML checks join the file.\[5,2\]


-


**Goes past the spread.** It applies your credit policy, drafts the cited memo and integrates with any LOS, or runs as Intelligent LOS. SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001.\[2,3,7,8\]

Banks, credit unions, CDFIs and non-bank lenders that want the spread, the analysis and the memo in one platform.

-

Banks and credit unions replacing their lending system of record.

**Inside the system.** Automated Spreading is a feature of the origination system, so it reaches a lender through the platform.\[10\]

Banks and credit unions choosing a new loan origination system with spreading built in.

-


**Inside the suite.** Spreading is one step of a credit workflow that also covers origination, scoring and decisions.\[11\]

Banks that want spreading and scoring in one commercial credit suite.

Banks, credit unions and finance companies that want spreading inside one origination platform.

## Aloan


Best for community bank and credit union commercial desks that want cited spreads and memos


Aloan describes an AI-native commercial loan origination platform for community banks and credit unions. Its spreading covers 1040, 1065, 1120 and 1120-S returns and bank statements, with every number mapped to its source page.\[13\]


-


**Spread and ratios.** It reads skewed scans and handwritten amendments, and calculates DSCR, liquidity and custom ratios from the spread data.\[13\]


-


**Memo and fit.** It checks the deal against the bank’s written credit policy and drafts a memo. It runs as the commercial LOS or alongside yours, and says most lenders are live in 2 to 4 weeks.\[13,14\]


Best for:


Community banks and credit unions whose commercial desk wants spreading and memo drafting.

Best for SMB, equipment finance and broker-sourced deals that want spreads in their own Excel model


Kaaj calls itself an AI underwriting platform. Its spreading takes financial statements and tax returns from PDF, Excel or Word into the lender’s own Excel model, with policy-based add-back suggestions.\[15\]


-


**Statements and checks.** Its bank statement analysis reads digital and scanned PDFs, including phone scans, and its fraud page cites 25+ forensic signals per document.\[16,17\]


-


**Fit.** It runs beside your CRM or LOS, with a typical go-live of two to three weeks starting with a pilot, according to Kaaj.\[15,18\]

SMB, equipment finance and merchant cash advance lenders, and brokers, that want spreads in their own Excel model.

## MightyBot

MightyBot calls itself a policy-driven AI agent platform. Its spreading page says agents extract statements and tax returns, map line names to the lender’s template and keep every value linked to its source.\[19\]


-


**Policy on the spread.** The platform applies the lender’s written policy to the spread, and the same spread feeds ratios, covenant tests and credit memos.\[19\]


-


**Fit.** It works alongside your LOS, and its page puts typical delivery at about 60 days.\[19\]

Lenders that want policy tests and covenant monitoring fed by the spread.

FlashSpread, from BeSmartee, is a spreading product for commercial credit teams. It lists tax returns, financial statements, bank statements and K-1 ownership schedules among the documents it spreads.\[20\]


-


**Output.** It uses AI-assisted extraction on complex structured and unstructured documents, generates balance sheets, income statements, ratios and global cash flow reports, and traces values back to the source documents.\[20\]


-


**Fit.** It integrates with supported LOS platforms and is built for banks, credit unions and CDFIs.\[20\]


Best for:

## How do you choose financial spreading software?


Six questions separate these tools more than any feature list.


-


**Does it read your real tax returns?** Kita reads Form 1120 and 1120-S, Schedule C, K-1s, 1065 partnership returns and quarterly 941s.\[6\] Aloan spreads 1040, 1065, 1120 and 1120-S returns and traces K-1s, and Kaaj lists 1120, 1120-S, 1065 and 1040 with Schedules C, E and K-1.\[13,15\] Send each vendor a return with K-1s.


-


**Can it read the messy statement?** Kita reads PDFs, scans, photos and screenshots, with no template per layout.\[1\] Aloan reads skewed scans and handwritten amendments, and Kaaj reads phone scans.\[13,16\] Ask every vendor to read your worst recent file.


-


**Can you trace every figure?** Every figure in a Kita spread links to the document line that produced it, so an analyst can check any number against its source.\[1\] Aloan maps each number to its source page, and MightyBot keeps every value linked to its source.\[13,19\]


-


**Does it check the document before it spreads it?** A spread built on an edited statement is a faster route to the wrong answer. Kita Capture checks for tampering and metadata edits.\[5\] Kaaj’s fraud page cites 25+ forensic signals per document.\[17\]


-


**What happens after the spread?** Kita holds the file against your encoded credit policy, flags anything outside it and drafts a cited memo for your underwriter.\[2,3\] Aloan checks the deal against the bank’s written credit policy and drafts a memo.\[13\] A dedicated spreading product leaves those steps to another system.


-


**Does it fit your stack?** Kita integrates with any LOS or runs as Intelligent LOS, so the choice stays yours.\[2,7\] Abrigo, nCino and Baker Hill offer spreading inside their own origination systems, so using it means adopting the system.\[9,10,12\]


Our recommendation is Kita: it answers yes to all six and covers the whole file, then hands the booked loan to any servicing system. If you only need part of the job, the lending suites bring spreading with their own system, Aloan, Kaaj and MightyBot analyze documents beside your LOS, and FlashSpread does the spread alone.


## How do you test financial spreading software on your own files?


A demo on a clean sample proves little. Run the same five-step test on every tool on your shortlist.


-


**Pick five closed files** from the last year, with the spreads your analysts built.


-


**Make one messy:** a photographed statement, a scan with a missing page or a non-standard layout.


-


**Include a return with K-1s** and check that the ownership schedules land in the right rows.


-


**Add one known altered document** and see whether the tool catches it before it spreads the numbers.


-


**Compare the totals and ratios** with your analysts’ spread, and time each file from upload to a spread an underwriter can review.


Kita is set up with your own credit policy in under 24 hours. Aloan says most lenders go live in 2 to 4 weeks, Kaaj says two to three weeks after a pilot, and MightyBot’s page puts typical delivery at about 60 days.\[13,15,19\] Ask each vendor what the calendar depends on.

## Frequently asked questions


### What is the best financial spreading software?


Kita is the best financial spreading software for most lenders because it spreads every statement in one pass and then carries the file on: it reads tax returns, statements, ledgers and bank statements including scans and photos, cites every figure to its source line, checks the documents for tampering, applies your credit policy and drafts a cited credit memo, on every loan type. Abrigo, nCino, Moody’s CreditLens and Baker Hill offer spreading inside a lending system, Aloan, Kaaj and MightyBot focus on spreading and analysis beside your LOS, and FlashSpread is a dedicated spreading product. Run one of your closed files through Kita to see the result.


### What is financial spreading software, and how does it work?


Financial spreading is restating a borrower’s financial statements in one standard format, period by period, so a lender can compare them and compute ratios such as debt service coverage. Spreading software reads the borrower’s tax returns, statements and bank records, maps each line to the lender’s template and computes the ratios, so the analyst reviews a finished spread instead of retyping it. It does not replace the analyst: judgment calls such as how to treat an owner’s loan stay with a person, and the lender’s underwriter makes the decision.


### Which documents can financial spreading software read?


Most tools read tax returns and financial statements, and the better ones also read bank statements, ledgers and ownership schedules such as K-1s. Kita reads Form 1120 and 1120-S, Schedule C, K-1s, 1065 partnership returns and quarterly 941s, plus profit and loss statements, balance sheets, general ledgers, receivables aging and bank statements, as PDFs, scans, photos and screenshots, with no template per layout. Whichever tool you choose, give it your messiest recent file.


### Do we have to replace our loan origination system to get automated spreading?


No. Kita integrates with any external system, including any LOS, core, CRM, credit bureau, data provider, servicing or e-sign tool, and lenders that want one origination system can run the whole process in Kita’s Intelligent LOS. Aloan, Kaaj, MightyBot and FlashSpread also say they work alongside an existing LOS, while Abrigo, nCino and Baker Hill offer spreading as part of their own origination systems.


### How long does it take to set up financial spreading software, and how should we test it?


Kita is set up with your own credit policy in under 24 hours, and later changes ship just as fast. Aloan says most lenders go live in 2 to 4 weeks, Kaaj says two to three weeks after a pilot, and MightyBot’s page puts typical delivery at about 60 days. Whichever you choose, run five recent files through it, including one with a photographed statement, one with a known altered document and one with a K-1, and compare the spread with your analysts’ own.


### What is Kita and how does it handle financial spreading?


Kita is an end-to-end AI underwriting platform for lenders, and financial spreading is one of the things it does. Its AI Underwriter pulls statements, general ledgers and bank data into a normalized period-over-period spread, with every figure cited to the document line that produced it, then drafts a cited credit assessment against the lender’s own policy. Kita recommends; the lender’s underwriter decides.
